messages:
Mia: Heads up — I opened a docs PR to add a small migration note for Optimize quant profiles around short-sequence workloads. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4827
Sam: thanks Mia. Can you summarize the change in one sentence for the changelog?
Mia: quick summary: clarify that the legacy qprofile v0.9 tends to degrade QA short-contexts (<64 tokens), recommend qprofile-compact or dynamic-8 for these cases, and add a tiny sample corpus + SDK snippet showing kv-prefetch + batching.
Devon: Is the sample corpus going to be public or internal? we should avoid exposing PII.
Mia: public synthetic phrases + shortQA.json (100 pairs) — all synthetic, no PII. I put the file under docs/examples/optimize/shortseq-sample.json in the PR.
Ashley: re: SDK snippet — can we show both the JS and Python minimal examples? PMs keep asking for simple copy-paste.
Mia: yep. I added a JS example, still need the Python one and a snippet that toggles kv-prefetch + batch_size.
Sam: I can draft the Python snippet. What runtime config do we want to recommend for the snippet? keep it conservative so it works on Hosted.
Mia: recommend: model: "redwood/opt-mini-1.0", max_tokens: 64, batch_size: 8, kv_prefetch: true, quant_profile: "qprofile-compact" and show fallbacks.
Devon: small nit — in the migration section we should call out the behavior change: latency can improve but you might see score drift on outlier prompts. Add an example eval command.
Mia: good call. I'll add an eval command using the sample corpus and show how to compute exact-match delta.
Sam: here's the Python snippet I drafted — pls sanity-check and paste into the PR:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(
  model="redwood/opt-mini-1.0",
  inputs=["What is the capital of France?"],
  max_tokens=64,
  batch_size=8,
  kv_prefetch=True,
  quant_profile="qprofile-compact"
)
print(resp[0].text)
```
Mia: looks good. Could you also include the param mapping for our HTTP API form (so users who use curl can follow)?
Sam: added a short curl example inline in the PR description.
Oliver: docs-bot just finished a preview deploy: https://redwood-docs-pr-preview.netlify.app/pr/4827 — quick link to check layout. :rocket:
docs-bot: Preview build succeeded (netlify) — site: /pr/4827 — 6 files changed, 2 new assets.
Ashley: I noticed one UX thing — the quant profiles table is long. Can we add a condensed 'quick-reco' callout box at the top for newbies? e.g., "Short sequences (<64): qprofile-compact | Medium (64–512): dynamic-8 | Long (>512): dynamic-4"
Mia: yes I can add that callout and link down to the detailed table.
Devon: when you add the evaluation example, please include the exact commands we use in infra so QE can reproduce: `python tools/eval_corpus.py --model redwood/opt-mini-1.0 --quant qprofile-compact --corpus examples/optimize/shortseq-sample.json`
Mia: will add. Also adding a short note about rolling back: how to pin to legacy qprofile if you see regressions.
Sam: who should be the final reviewer? I'd nominate @Ashley for UX + @Devon for eval bits.
Mia: tagging both in the PR. Also adding a tiny migration checklist in the doc: 1) run eval corpus, 2) compare EM/ROUGE, 3) toggle kv_prefetch, 4) if regressions, pin quant_profile to legacy.
Ashley: +1. One more tiny ask — can we add a one-line line-to-line diff example showing tokenization changes that cause drift? helps explain why short answers flip sometimes.
Mia: good idea, I'll add a short snippet showing token id shift.
Oliver: quick reminder — close window for docs bugfix patch today at 18:00 PT or it gets deferred to next cycle.
Mia: chasing final reviews now. Thanks everyone :pray: 
Sam: reviewed and left a small nit about wording in the curl example.
Mia: fixed the nit and pushed. 
Oliver: docs-bot: Preview updated — build passed.
Mia: marking this as ready-to-merge if no objections.
Ashley: merging after CI green. :thumbsup:
Mia: merged! I'll open a follow-up issue to track telemetry for shortseq regressions and link it in the doc.
